title: Finite and algebraic general linear groups
notes: The page writes \(G=GL_n(k)\), \(|k|=q\), and \(\underline G=GL(\bar k)\).
statement: For a finite field \(k=\mathbb F_q\) and an integer \(n\ge1\), let \(\mathbf G=GL_{n,\bar k}\). Then \(G=\mathbf G(\bar k)^F=GL_n(k)\), where \(F\) raises entries to the \(q\)-th power.

statement: For smooth real \(u\), as formal differential operators, \([A_0,L]=u_x\) and \([A_1,L]=u_{xxx}-6uu_x\). Thus \(L_t=[A_1,L]\) gives \(u_t=u_{xxx}-6uu_x\); reversing the commutator reverses time.

title: The real periodic Schrödinger operator is self-adjoint
notes: Gelfand writes \(y^{\prime\prime}+uy=\lambda y\), real periodic \(u\), and says the closure from \(C_c^\infty\) is self-adjoint.
statement: For real smooth \(T\)-periodic \(u\), the operator \(-D^2+u\) on \(C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)\) is essentially self-adjoint in \(L^2(\mathbb R)\); its closure has domain \(H^2(\mathbb R)\).

notes: For every phase \(t\), \(y(x+T)=e^{it}y(x)\) and \(y_x(x+T)=e^{it}y_x(x)\) define a self-adjoint discrete-spectrum problem.

title: Gelfand transform and its normalization
notes: The lemma writes an integral reconstruction, a quasiperiodicity condition, and an \(L^2\) identity, but mixes period 1 and \(2\pi\), integrates over \(dx\) instead of phase, and drops one subscript.
statement: For \(f\in L^2(\mathbb R)\), define \(Uf(\theta,x)=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}e^{-im\theta}f(x+mT)\) first for compactly supported smooth \(f\), then by completion. It satisfies \(Uf(\theta,x+T)=e^{i\theta}Uf(\theta,x)\), \(f(x)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}Uf(\theta,x)\,d\theta\), and \(\|f\|_2^2=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^T|Uf|^2\,dx\,d\theta\). The identities hold in the corresponding \(L^2\) spaces.
reconstruction: The transform itself and a consistent normalization are supplied; the manuscript's three defective displayed identities are retained in the corrections table.
fate: The notes explicitly credit Gelfand's circa-1950 Doklady paper. The concrete normalization here follows Fourier-series Parseval; it is an editorial reconstruction of a classical unitary direct-integral transform. \citet[\S1]{novikov1974periodic} uses the resulting band decomposition.

title: Bloch eigenfunction expansion and band derivatives
notes: Each \(f_t\) is expanded in \(y_{t,n}\), with coefficients written without a complex conjugate; the notes then mention computing \(d\lambda/dt\).
statement: Choose an orthonormal eigenbasis \(\phi_{n,\theta}\) of each fiber. Then \(Uf(\theta,\cdot)=\sum_n\langle Uf,\phi_{n,\theta}\rangle\phi_{n,\theta}\) in \(L^2(0,T)\), with the complex conjugate in the inner product. If \(\lambda_n(\theta)\) is simple, gauge to periodic \(v=e^{-i\theta x/T}\phi\); then \(\lambda^{\prime}_n(\theta)=\langle v,[-2iT^{-1}(D+i\theta/T)]v\rangle\) for normalized \(v\).

title: Monodromy in a conjugate solution basis
notes: With \(\lambda=k^2\), initial data \((y,y_x)=(1,ik)\), the pair \(y,\bar y\) gives \(T=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\\bar b&\bar a\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), \(|a|^2-|b|^2=1\).

Its half trace \(d(\lambda)=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}T=\operatorname{Re}a\) is independent of the basepoint and extends as an entire function of \(\lambda\).

title: Floquet multipliers and spectral bands
notes: The multipliers are \(a_R\pm\sqrt{a_R^2-1}\); bounded solutions are equated to \(|a_R|\le1\), and outside the strip the notes write \(e^{\pm t}\).
statement: For real \(\lambda\), the multipliers solve \(\rho^2-2d(\lambda)\rho+1=0\), and \(\sigma(L)=\{\lambda:|d(\lambda)|\le1\}\). Inside an open band all solutions are bounded. At a band edge at least one nonzero bounded periodic or antiperiodic solution exists, but the second solution can grow linearly. In a gap the real multipliers are \(\pm e^{\pm\kappa}\), with a common minus sign when \(d<-1\).

notes: Novikov says monotonicity was proved for small potentials; Gelfand announces a \ru{конкурс на доказательство} for the next meeting.

notes: For constant \(u\), Gelfand says the spectrum is positive. The later free matrix has diagonal entries \(e^{\pm iT}\) and \(a_R=\cos T\), omitting spectral dependence.

title: Mathieu stability sketch
notes: The equation is \(-y^{\prime\prime}+(a+b\cos2x)y=0\); the first stability band is associated with \(a+b\cos2x<0\), followed by a contrast with constant coefficients.
statement: For each real \((a,b)\), stability of the Mathieu equation is governed by the trace of its period-\(\pi\) monodromy: at least one bounded solution exists precisely when its half trace has absolute value at most one. The inequality in the notes does not specify whether it is pointwise, averaged, or a statement along a parameter curve, and does not identify an exact first-band boundary.
reconstruction: Only the well-defined monodromy criterion is supplied as context; the sketch is not promoted to a new theorem.
fate: Floquet stability is classical; \citet[\S1]{novikov1974periodic} supports the trace criterion. No exact publication match is claimed for the ambiguous inequality or sketch.

title: Closed gaps and double boundary eigenvalues
notes: Periodic and antiperiodic points have \(|a_R|=1\); a double degeneracy has \(b(x_0,\lambda_n)\equiv0\).
statement: For real periodic scalar \(L\), a closed finite gap is a double eigenvalue of the relevant periodic or antiperiodic problem. Its monodromy is \(M=\pm I\); in any admissible conjugate basis \(b=0\). At an open-gap edge the boundary eigenvalue is simple and \(M\) is a nontrivial Jordan matrix with eigenvalue \(\pm1\).

title: Which supplementary data determine a periodic potential?
notes: The half trace does not determine \(u\). The notes ask which scattering data beyond the spectrum do, mentioning Dubrovin and Faddeev's students.
statement: At a fixed basepoint, supplement the band spectrum of a real smooth finite-gap Schrödinger operator with its Dirichlet divisor: one point on each real gap oval of the hyperelliptic spectral curve, including its sheet, with the usual endpoint identification. These data determine the potential. Band edges alone leave an isospectral family and cannot even distinguish translations.
reconstruction: The finite-gap restriction and sheet-labelled divisor are added explicitly; no unrestricted theorem is inferred solely from the finite-gap reference.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--3]{novikov1974periodic} develops the stationary spectral curve. \citet[Chapter~2, \S3, pp.~84--87 of the Russian original, especially Eqs.~(2.3.11)--(2.3.12)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} gives one sheet-labelled pole on each gap oval, its evolution, and the trace formula reconstructing the potential. These pages were read. The latter paper was received 2 June 1975 and published in 1976. This is an exact answer in the finite-gap scope, a partial match to the notes' unrestricted periodic wording.

title: Finite-gap periodic potentials
notes: Eventually all boundary eigenvalues become double and the forbidden intervals shrink to points.
statement: A real smooth periodic potential is finite-gap if only finitely many bounded complementary intervals of \(\sigma(-D^2+u)\) are nonempty. Equivalently, all sufficiently high periodic/antiperiodic pairs coincide. The half-line below the bottom of the spectrum is not counted as a finite gap.
fate: \citet[\S2]{novikov1974periodic} uses this precise spectral class.

title: Stationary KdV and finite-gap spectra
notes: If \([A,L]=P(u,\ldots)\) is multiplication and \(P=0\) has a periodic solution, the potential is finite-gap; the converse is also asserted. The next page specifies one operator at every odd order and their linear combinations.
statement: For real smooth periodic \(u\), a nontrivial odd-order differential operator \(A\) commuting with \(L=-D^2+u\), with nonzero constant leading coefficient, forces finitely many open gaps. Conversely a smooth real periodic finite-gap potential satisfies a stationary equation of the KdV hierarchy. A trivial commuting operator \(A=p(L)\) is not a sufficient hypothesis.
reconstruction: The indispensable odd-order/nontrivial condition is obtained from the following page, not from the isolated theorem sentence. The converse is separated from the forward theorem.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2.1 and its stationary construction, pp.~59--62]{novikov1974periodic} is the near-contemporary primary publication. The finite-gap inverse and converse framework is developed in \citet{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The converse is explicitly proved in Chapter~2, \S3, statement3, p.~86 of the Russian original of \citet{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}, which was also read.

title: Finite-dimensional Hamiltonian stationary flows
notes: The stationary hierarchy equations are Hamiltonian systems with \(n\) degrees of freedom and a maximal set of commuting integrals.
statement: Fix a nondegenerate stationary KdV equation of order \(2n+1\) and integrate its translation-invariant first integral once. On the resulting regular \(2n\)-dimensional phase space, the induced finite-dimensional flow has a Hamiltonian structure and \(n\) independent commuting integrals on a regular open set. Singular levels and loss of independence are not covered by the Liouville-torus conclusion.
reconstruction: The regular-level and independence qualifications distinguish Liouville integrability from a claim about every singular point.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2.1, pp.~59--61]{novikov1974periodic} supplies the stationary Hamiltonian systems and commuting integrals; manuscript received 18 February 1974.

title: Density of finite-gap potentials
notes: Novikov asks \ru{любой ли потенциал аппроксим. конечнозонными?}; neither function space nor topology is stated.
statement: For every real \(q\in H^m(\mathbb R/T\mathbb Z)\), \(m\ge0\), and every \(\varepsilon>0\), does a real periodic finite-gap \(q_*\) exist with \(\|q-q_*\|_{H^m}<\varepsilon\)? Yes. In particular smooth periodic potentials can be approximated in any prescribed finite collection of Sobolev seminorms.
reconstruction: The periodic setting comes from the talk; the real Sobolev topology and quantifiers are an explicit modern formulation, not written in the notebook.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.2 and its proof in \S5]{grebertkappelerposchel2004gaps} proves finite-gap density in \(H^m\), \(m\ge0\), attributes the question to Novikov, and credits the first proof to Marchenko--Ostrovskii's 1975 characterization of Hill spectra. The author-hosted full PDF was downloaded and these passages read. The manuscript was received 15 September 2003, revised in 2004, and published in 2004. First-proof credit is distinguished from the later proof actually inspected.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Affirmatively settled in every real Sobolev space \(H^m\), \(m\ge0\); it is not a C/D candidate.

title: A stationary matrix equation and its spectral polynomial
notes: A traceless \(2\times2\) matrix \(\Lambda\) satisfies \(\Lambda^{\prime}=[\Lambda,Q]\). Its eigenvalues are written \(\pm\sqrt{\det\Lambda}\), followed by the words the word polynomial.
statement: For any differentiable traceless matrix solution \(\Lambda_x=[\Lambda,Q]\), its characteristic polynomial is \(\mu^2+\det\Lambda\); hence \(\mu=\pm\sqrt{-\det\Lambda}\) and \(\det\Lambda\) is independent of \(x\). In the stationary KdV construction a suitable gauge and spectral parameter yield polynomial coefficients of the spectral curve. The square roots themselves are generally algebraic functions, not polynomials.
reconstruction: The notes mix \(\delta\), \(\delta^2\), and a \(\delta^{-1}\) gauge term; no exact matrix-degree assertion is recovered without fixing that gauge. The polynomial claim is safely assigned to the determinant/spectral polynomial.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~61--62]{novikov1974periodic} constructs the matrix and spectral polynomial. The sign follows independently from the characteristic polynomial of a traceless \(2\times2\) matrix.

title: Riccati expansion and conservation-law densities
notes: \(\psi_k=e^{ikx+\int_{-\infty}^x\chi}\), \(\chi=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_nk^{-n}\), and \(I_n=\int_{\mathbb R}\chi_n\) are conserved.
statement: For a nonvanishing local solution of \(-\psi_{xx}+u\psi=k^2\psi\), put \(\psi^{\prime}/\psi=ik+\chi\). Then \(\chi_x+2ik\chi+\chi^2=u\), which recursively determines a formal Laurent series with differential-polynomial coefficients. Under smooth rapid decay its convergent spatial density integrals are KdV conservation laws; for periodic \(u\) use one-period integrals of the densities. The formal expansion need not converge in \(k^{-1}\).
reconstruction: The notes temporarily use the decaying-line normalization inside a periodic discussion. We separate the two regimes and do not integrate a nondecaying periodic density over the whole line.
fate: \citet[trace identities and conservation laws]{zakharovfaddeev1971kdv} already develops this connection in 1971; it also matches the earlier occurrence 1970-219.6. \citet[\S2]{novikov1974periodic} adapts the hierarchy to periodic potentials.

title: Evolution of a normalized eigenfunction basis
notes: \(\dot\psi=A\psi+\lambda\psi+\mu\bar\psi\), with \(\Lambda\) formed from the last two coefficients.
statement: If \(L_t=[A,L]\) and \((L-k^2)\psi=0\), then \((L-k^2)(\psi_t-A\psi)=0\). In a two-dimensional fundamental solution space, the difference is a linear combination of basis solutions; the coefficients depend on time and spectral parameter but not on the spatial variable in that fixed basis. They enforce the chosen initial-data normalization.

title: Monodromy conjugation under time and basepoint changes
notes: \(\dot T=[\Lambda,T]\), \(T_{x_0}=[Q,T]\), followed by the stationary equation \(\Lambda^{\prime}=[\Lambda,Q]\).
statement: For a smooth periodic Lax system with compatible auxiliary operator, the period monodromy evolves by conjugation under time evolution and under moving the basepoint. With a consistently chosen fundamental matrix the equations are commutator equations, so trace, determinant, and multipliers are invariant. The sign of the displayed commutator depends on whether the basis or coordinate vectors are propagated.

title: Finite spectral curve and band edges
notes: For stationary solutions, ``band edges are the roots of a polynomial.
statement: For a regular finite-gap potential with \(g\) open gaps, the reduced hyperelliptic curve can be written \(\mu^2=\prod_{j=0}^{2g}(\lambda-E_j)\). Its simple branch points are the bottom endpoint and the endpoints of the open gaps. Infinitely many closed-gap double points of the full discriminant are not distinct roots of this finite reduced polynomial.
reconstruction: The reduction by double factors is essential: a finite polynomial cannot list every high periodic/antiperiodic double eigenvalue.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~61--62]{novikov1974periodic} obtains the algebraic spectral polynomial. The reduced-curve terminology is a modern clarification.

title: Constructing the odd KdV hierarchy
notes: Gelfand asks how to find \(A_n=D^{2n+1}+\cdots\) such that \([A_n,-D^2+u]\) is multiplication, how the resulting \(P_n\) are related, and how this connects with trace formulas and other equations.
statement: In the formal algebra of differential polynomials in a scalar smooth potential, odd-order differential operators can be chosen recursively so that \([A_n,L]\) has order zero. They are determined up to lower hierarchy flows and scalar polynomials in \(L\), after a leading normalization is fixed. The multiplication coefficients are the KdV hierarchy; the Riccati recursion supplies its conserved densities. The question about other equations is answered here only for the displayed dressing examples.

title: Gelfand--Levitan equation and Volterra factorization
notes: \(K+F+\int_x^\infty K(x,s)F(s,y)\,ds=0\), and \(1+\hat F=(1+\hat K_+)^{-1}(1+\hat K_-)\), with opposite triangular supports.
statement: For sufficiently smooth, decaying scalar or matrix kernels, suppose each restricted integral equation on \([x,\infty)\) is invertible and the corresponding Volterra operators are well-defined. Solving the equation for \(y\ge x\) gives the upper triangular factor \(K_+\); multiplication determines a lower triangular remainder \(K_-\). Conversely such an invertible factorization gives that kernel equation. An unsigned integral bound on \(F\) alone does not guarantee invertibility.

title: Kernel commutators and formal adjoints
notes: Equation (4) has an obliterated sign; equation (5) prints a plus sign. The bottom line identifies \(K_{xx}-K_{yy}\) with \([\hat K,D^2]\). Later formulas use an adjoint superscript inconsistently.
statement: For a full-line smooth rapidly decaying kernel, the kernel of \([D^n,F]\) is \(\partial_x^nF-(-1)^n\partial_y^nF\). More generally \([A,F]\) has kernel \(A_xF-A_y^{\mathrm t}F\), with the formal transpose acting in the second variable. For triangular kernels there are additional diagonal boundary terms, absorbed in the dressed coefficients. Thus the displayed second-order difference corresponds to \([D^2,\hat K]\), not the reversed commutator.
reconstruction: The missing sign is reconstructed by integration by parts, not deciphered from overwritten ink. Formal transpose is distinguished from Hermitian adjoint for complex/matrix kernels.
